answer: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) works by allowing an adversary to embed malicious scripts into content that is served to web browsers. The primary goal of the attack is for the client-side browser to execute the injected script with the user's privilege level. This type of attack exploits vulnerabilities in programs that permit remote hosts to execute code and scripts. For instance, an attacker can inject scripts into user-generated content on platforms like bulletin boards or blogs, which can then be echoed back to other users' browsers, potentially bypassing security controls in place [Source 2][Source 3].
